 Cavan Sullivan leads Philadelphia Union into playoffs: "He's not afraid"
 Charles Boehm
 Copy URL 
 Share on Facebook 
 Share on X 
 Cavan Sullivan has the world at his feet.
 The Philadelphia Union ’s 17-year-old wunderkind spearheaded his team’s dramatic resurrection from last place in the Eastern Conference to Audi 2026 MLS Cup Playoffs contenders, with the club looking like a highly dangerous lower seed heading into their Round One Best-of-3 Series opener vs. the New England Revolution at Gillette Stadium on Saturday afternoon (2 pm ET |  Apple TV ).
 Sullivan's 9g/14a set a new MLS record for most goal contributions by a teenager, making him a favorite for the Young Player of the Year award, as well as a key protagonist to watch in the postseason.
 Might he even be the final piece to the puzzle for a club who’ve won two Supporters’ Shields and reached the 2022 MLS Cup final, only to fall agonizingly short again and again?
 “The thing is, he has the personality for that,” interim head coach Ryan Richter told MLSsoccer.com. “He has the mentality. He's not afraid of the moment. He's excited by it, and he has the personality to take the pressure that comes with that and perform.”
 Big expectations
 Sullivan’s homegrown contract with the Union is reportedly the largest of its kind in MLS history, and is said to segue into a move to English titans Manchester City when he’s 18. Those adidas cleats he sports on game day are also custom, cutting-edge 3D-printed prototypes worn by only a handful of athletes on Earth.
 He just took part in his second US men’s national team camp, having become the youngest goalscorer in program history with his jaw-dropping golazo in last month’s friendly win over bitter rivals Mexico.
 You could be forgiven for wondering how it doesn’t all go to his head, how such a precociously talented kid could stay humble under such circumstances.
 Perhaps the best place to begin answering those concerns is Cavan’s morning commute to the Union’s training facility in Chester, Pennsylvania, and daily conversations en route with his older brother (and teammate) Quinn , and their paternal grandmother Kathleen.
 “Every day when we get in the car, we call her, and usually do a group call now,” Quinn explained to MLSsoccer.com last week.
 Cavan drives solo nowadays, since Quinn moved out of the family home earlier this year to get a taste of downtown living. But they still connect on the phone, then patch in Grandma, a “legendary English teacher,” in the words of the school’s social-media posts, for many years at local institution St. Joseph's Prep.
 “She carries the conversation with questions; she's got the teacher mode, so she's got all the questions lined up,” Quinn added. “But it's great to talk to her every day, and she says it makes her day. So that's really what it’s all about.
 “We're very family-oriented people, and that's another thing that we have together.”
 The City of Brotherly Goals! ❤️
Quinn Sullivan assists Cavan Sullivan to help extend the @PhilaUnion lead! pic.twitter.com/7470A1Bmus 
— Major League Soccer (@MLS) November 7, 2026 
 Strong support system
 For decades, the United States’ soccer community has waited and hoped for a legit superstar in the men’s game, a prodigy blessed enough to push both the USMNT and the sport as a whole to new heights. When someone with such potential arises, the likes of Landon Donovan, Freddy Adu, Christian Pulisic or, well, Cavan, a corresponding angst about the dangers of hype and excessive expectations inevitably follows.
 Despite such hubbub simmering around him since elementary school, Cavan kept on course, methodically climbing the developmental ladder before turning 2026 into his breakout year, nurtured by the Union’s league-leading youth system and a sturdy support structure on and off the pitch.
 “I mean, he's definitely had to mature quickly. That's not a secret,” noted Quinn, himself a game-breaking attacker who’s returned to form after last year’s torn ACL. 
 “But he knew what he signed up for. We grew up knowing that if this is what you want, you're not going to be the kid, and that he was OK with that. He's gotten to the point that he's at because of that dedication and because of that maturing, and dealing with the different environments that he was in.”
 The youngest of the Sullivans’ four children has shown special abilities since his toddler stage, and those around him seem to have found the right balance in allowing it to blossom. It helps that parents Brendan and Heike were both accomplished players in their own right, part of a multi-generational soccer clan that also includes Brendan’s father Larry, who coached Villanova University’s men’s team and other prominent local programs for decades.
 “The reminder, always, is what got him here,” said Richter, who has coached Cavan since his earliest days in the academy. “And it's a lot of hard work that got him here. Of course he has the talent, he has the support system, and he has the personality, but he works very hard for everything that's coming to him.
 “I'm so happy for him and proud of him, because I've seen the hard work, I've seen the patience, and now to be rewarded by putting together performances and the attention that comes with that, he deserves all of that.”
 The kid continues to shine ⭐
Cavan Sullivan is a finalist for @MLS MVP and Young Player of the Year! pic.twitter.com/2iCJei3d3i 
— Philadelphia Union (@PhilaUnion) November 12, 2026 
 Waiting his turn
 Richter is quick to point out that this blue-chip youngster hasn’t had it all handed to him.
 Cavan had to grind quietly and bide his time since signing a historic first-team deal in May 2024 , proving particularly patient under previous head coach Bradley Carnell, who led the Union to the 2025 Supporters’ Shield and seemed determined to keep Sullivan on a carefully throttled timeline.
 “That's the part that people, I think, don't give enough credit for,” said Richter. “Even though he's a young player, he went through his own version of adversity over the past two years.”
 Then there’s Cavan’s teammates. He had to win them over like any other new kid, though with so many other academy products on the roster, many had already played with him in the past. That’s cultivated both a respect for his skill and bravery, and a familiarity that keeps him grounded.
 “I think ‘banter’ is the right way to say it,” said Quinn. “In terms of the locker room, it's not a problem for him; he belongs. The guys love him. The guys joke with him, and he'll joke right back. He's got the youngest child mentality with three older brothers, so he had to fight for a lot.
 “People know that he has different qualities, and he's going to try s--t that might not work in training,” Quinn continued, joking that even he will occasionally “bicker” with his brother in the heat of competition. “You know he's going to probably do something to create a goal or an assist or a big chance in the game on the weekend – you eat that in training. But guys will still hit him with a, ‘dude, what was that?’”
 Cavan Sullivan: Dawg. 😤 pic.twitter.com/5meLIBQG4T 
— Major League Soccer (@MLS) October 4, 2026 
 USMNT future
 It’s much the same with the USMNT.
 When he reported to his first camp in September, Cavan had to step onto a stool and sing a song, a cappella, in front of the entire group, just like every other newbie. He picked ’Every Breath You Take,’ The Police’s 1980s classic – perhaps fitting given its themes of obsessive surveillance in the name of love – and later fielded a question about his phenom status with a veteran’s composure.
 “I've always said it: I don’t really focus too much on the noise off the field,” Cavan said. “I could just say my experiences both with the Union and the national team have been amazing. Whether you want to go with the ‘little brother’ narrative side of things, I don't mind it. I don't mind them sort of taking me under their wing.
 “My mentality just remains the same no matter where I go, and I feel like I'm a pretty driven person, and just focused on getting better and reaching my potential.”
 CAVAN SULLIVAN SCORES IN HIS FIRST USA-MEXICO GAME 😤
He's now the USMNT's youngest ever goalscorer. pic.twitter.com/uV4i6g26hO 
— B/R Football (@brfootball) October 4, 2026 
 Playoffs next
 Cavan’s first playoffs experience was limited to just two substitute appearances totaling 15 minutes last season, when the Union suffered a Conference Semifinal upset at the hands of New York City FC . Though he picked up a knock in their 4-1 Decision Day rout of Toronto FC that limited his playing time with the national team, he’ll almost certainly be the creative force that powers Philly’s Cinderella dreams.
 “This team definitely has the fight, the grit, the belief and the energy that it takes to make a deep run and win an MLS Cup,” said his brother Quinn, pointing to their charge up the standings under Richter and a collective motivation to deliver a trophy for retiring legend Alejandro Bedoya .
 “It's going to take everyone firing on all cylinders,” he added, “[but] we have a great opportunity to be a team that no one wants to play.”
